extracted.intended_audience: Users/developers of the Isabelle/Isar proof assistant (Isabelle/HOL users, proof engineers, tool integrators)
extracted.subtask_description: A technical quick-reference for Isabelle/Isar proof commands, code-generation commands, proof methods, attributes, proof-script primitives, and predefined symbols. It documents syntax forms and the intended behavior/semantics of commands and facilities used to write, inspect, and generate code from Isabelle theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: code_reserved
rubrics_metrics.description: Declares a list of names as reserved for a given target, preventing it to be shadowed by any generated code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to ensure certain identifiers are not overwritten by code generation for a specific target language/target; declare all names that generated code must not reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: code_printing
rubrics_metrics.description: Associates a series of symbols (constants, type constructors, classes, class relations, instances, module names) with target-specific serializations; omitting a serialization deletes an existing serialization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to provide or change how Isabelle symbols are serialized for a target (e.g., pretty-printed names in generated code). Removing a serialization entry will delete an existing mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: code_monad
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides an auxiliary mechanism to generate monadic code for Haskell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare monadic translations and helpers to produce Haskell-style monadic code when exporting Isabelle definitions to Haskell.

rubrics_metrics.name: code_identifier
rubrics_metrics.description: Associates a series of symbols (constants, type constructors, classes, class relations, instances, module names) with target-specific hints how these symbols shall be named. These hints gain precedence over names for symbols with no hints at all. Conflicting hints are subject to name disambiguation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use identifier hints to control generated names. Warning: the user is responsible to ensure that name prefixes of identifiers in compound statements (e.g., type classes or datatypes) remain consistent — conflicting hints may be disambiguated automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: code_reflect
rubrics_metrics.description: Without a "file_prefix" argument compiles code into the system runtime environment and modifies the code generator setup that future invocations of system runtime code generation referring to one of the "datatypes" or "functions" entities use these precompiled entities. With a "file_prefix" argument, the corresponding code is generated/exported to the specified file (as for export_code) without modifying the code generator setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use code_reflect to precompile and register code for runtime use, or to export generated code to a file by supplying file_prefix. Be aware of whether the code generator setup is modified (no file_prefix) or remains unchanged (with file_prefix).

rubrics_metrics.name: code_pred
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates code equations for a predicate given a set of introduction rules. Optional mode annotations determine which arguments are supposed to be input or output. If alternative introduction rules are declared, one must prove a corresponding elimination rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to obtain executable equations for predicates (so they can be used in code generation). Provide mode annotations to indicate input/output positions; ensure elimination rules exist when alternatives are declared.

rubrics_metrics.name: code_timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Scrapes timing samples from different stages of the code generator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for profiling the code generation pipeline to find and diagnose slow stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: code_simp_trace
rubrics_metrics.description: Traces the simplifier when it is used with code equations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable to debug simplification steps that occur during code equation generation or application.

rubrics_metrics.name: code_runtime_trace
rubrics_metrics.description: Traces ML code generated dynamically for execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to inspect or debug dynamically generated ML runtime code; helpful when diagnosing runtime behavior of generated code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main proof-command grammar (theorem/lemma/proposition forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Main document forms and theorems: notepad / begin ... end constructs; theorem/lemma/proposition declarations with optional 'fixes', 'assumes', 'shows'/'obtains' clauses and different proof forms. The grammar indicates that a proof is refinement* followed by a proper_proof, where proper_proof may be 'proof method? statement* qed method?' or 'done'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the grammar when structuring proofs: use 'fixes/assumes/shows' etc. to declare variables and facts, use refine/apply steps (refinements) and finish with proof blocks (qed/done). Use the documented theorem forms appropriate to whether you need 'obtains' or 'for' clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primitive proof commands (fix, assume, then, have, show, using, unfolding, proof, qed, done, { ... }, next, note, let, write, show/have variants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primitives used inside proofs: e.g., 'fix x' — augment context by x; 'assume a: A' — add assumption; 'then' — indicate forward chaining; 'have/show' — prove local results; 'using'/'unfolding' — indicate use of facts or unfolding definitions; 'proof ... qed' / 'done' — indicate proof structure and completion; '{ ... }' explicit blocks; 'next' to switch proof blocks; 'note' to record facts; 'let' to abbreviate terms; 'write' to declare local mixfix syntax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these primitives to shape the proof state and context. 'fix' and 'assume' establish local variables and hypotheses; 'then' forwards facts; use 'unfolding' to enable definitional rewrites; structure proofs with explicit blocks and use 'next' to proceed between subproofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations and synonyms in proofs (by, .., ., from a, with a, from this)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviations map longer proof idioms to shorter forms: 'by m1 m2 ≡ proof m1 qed m2', '.. ≡ by standard', '. ≡ by this', 'from a ≡ note a then', 'with a ≡ from a and this', 'from this ≡ then'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the abbreviations to write concise proof scripts. Understand their equivalences to full proof constructs when reading or refactoring proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derived proof elements (also, finally, moreover, ultimately, presume, define, consider, obtain, presume forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Higher-level proof macros/aliases: e.g., 'also' relates calculations, 'finally' finishes them; 'moreover/ultimately' combine facts; 'presume' ≈ 'assume'; 'define x where x = t' ≈ 'fix ... assume ...'; 'consider/obtain' provide structured ways to introduce witnesses or case splits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use derived elements to express common proof patterns (calculations, chaining facts, introducing witnesses) succinctly and readably; they are equivalences to more primitive commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic/printing commands (print type/typ, print term/term, print proposition/prop, print fact/thm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands for inspecting the proof environment: 'print type' / 'typ τ' to show types, 'print term' / 'term t' for terms, 'print proposition' / 'prop ϕ', 'print fact' / 'thm a' to display facts; 'print_statement a' prints fact in long statement form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these diagnostics to investigate types, terms, and theorems during development and debugging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof methods: single-step, repeated, and automated tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorized proof methods: Single steps (assumption, this, rule a, standard, contradiction, cases t, induct x) for applying individual inferences; Repeated steps (intro, intro_classes, intro_locales, unfold_locales, elim, unfold a) for inserting many facts; Automated tools (iprover, blast, fast, simp/simp_all, auto, force) plus specialized ones (arith, meson, metis, iprover) and combined strategies (Simplifier + Classical Reasoner, arithmetic procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose methods based on proof needs: use single-step methods when controlling refinement; repeated/intro/elim for batch transformations; automated tools for high-level automation. Combine simp with classical reasoner for many goals; use arith/linarith for arithmetic reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes (OF, of, where, symmetric, THEN, rule_format, elim_format, simp, intro, elim, dest, iiff, split, trans, sym, case split, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes modify the behavior of rules and declarations: e.g., 'OF a' resolves a rule with facts, 'where x = t' instantiates with terms, 'symmetric' applies symmetry; declaration attributes include 'simp' (simplifier rule), 'intro/elim/dest' (insertion into rule sets), 'iiff', 'split', 'trans', 'sym', 'case split'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach attributes to lemmas/theorems to control how tools (simp, auto, classical reasoner) use them. Use appropriate attributes to ensure rules are available to the intended tools and in the intended form (e.g., rule_format, elim_format).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule declarations and method selection (rule, iprover, blast, fast, simp, simp_all, auto, force and their applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common declarative and procedural methods for using/declaring rules: 'rule' applies a rule, 'iprover/blast/fast' are higher-level provers, 'simp' family for rewriting, 'auto/force' for combined strategies. The manual lists which attributes/methods pair well with different kinds of rules (e.g., Pure.elim!/Pure.intro!, elim/intro, simp/cong/split etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When declaring rules, consider how they will be used by methods: mark them as simp or intro/elim accordingly. Select the method appropriate to the rule style and goal shape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof-script commands and tactics for backward refinement (apply, apply_end, supply, subgoal, defer, prefer, back, done, cut_tac, drule_tac, erule_tac, rule_tac, insert, thin_tac, rename_tac, rotate_tac, raw_tactic, tactic text, induction/case_tac)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands and tactics for interactive proof construction: 'apply' to perform backward-refinement steps; 'apply_end' for terminal position; 'supply' to add facts; 'subgoal' to start nested proofs; 'defer'/'prefer' to reorder subgoals; 'back' to backtrack; 'done' to finish. Tactics include resolution/elim-resolution/drule_tac/erule_tac/frule_tac/cut_tac/insert/thin_tac/subgoal_tac/rename_tac/rotate_tac/induction/induct_tac/case_tac and arbitrary ML tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these commands to manipulate subgoals and perform fine-grained proof refinement. Reserve raw tactics and ML tactics for cases where higher-level methods do not suffice; use 'defer'/'prefer' to manage subgoal ordering during complex proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predefined Isabelle symbols and notation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Isabelle supports an infinite number of non-ASCII symbols represented as \<name> in source. Predefined standard symbols (listed in the appendix) are available for document output and Isabelle/jEdit/LATEX. Single symbols may be prefixed by \^sup> (superscript) or \<^sub> (subscript), and many symbols can be printed in bold with \<^bold>. Sub- and superscripts that span regions can be marked with \<^bsub>...\<^esub> and \<^bsup>...\<^esup>, but typographic rendering quality is limited. Note: \<^sup>, \<^sub>, \<^bold> cannot be combined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the \<name> notation for non-ASCII symbols in source. Prefer the documented macros when preparing Isabelle documents or LATEX output. Beware of limitations (no combination of sup/sub/bold, typographic issues for region-wide subscripts/superscripts).
